question: In May 2025, the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) conducted combat firing (with reduced explosives) of the indigenous Multi-Influence Ground Mine with the _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Navy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted a combat firing trial of the indigenous **Multi-Influence Ground Mine** in collaboration with the **Indian Navy**.
 
• The test was carried out with **reduced explosives** to validate the sophisticated **sensor systems** and **triggering mechanisms** against the actual physical signatures of naval vessels without causing structural damage to the test platforms.
 
• This state-of-the-art underwater weapon has been designed and developed by the **Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL)**, a premier laboratory of **DRDO** located in **Visakhapatnam**.
 
• The **Multi-Influence Ground Mine** is a highly advanced sea mine that can be deployed from **ships** and **submarines** to protect Indian waters and deny sea access to enemy forces. ***Hence, the correct answer is the Indian Navy.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Multi-Influence Technology:** 
 
 
• Unlike traditional contact mines, influence mines do not require physical contact with a ship's hull. They use **microprocessor-based sensors** to detect **magnetic**, **acoustic**, and **pressure** signatures of passing vessels.
 
• The mine is **programmable**, allowing it to target specific types of ships or submarines while ignoring friendly vessels or decoys, making it a "smart" underwater weapon.
 
 
 
• **Design and Production:**
 
 
• The development of this mine is a significant step toward **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) in the defense sector, reducing the **Indian Navy's** reliance on imported naval mines.
 
• Following successful combat trials, the technology is typically transferred to production agencies like **Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL)** for mass manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Sea mines are cost-effective tools for **sea denial** and **harbor defense**. They can be laid in **shipping lanes** or near **enemy ports** to restrict their naval movement during a conflict.
 
• The **Multi-Influence Ground Mine** is designed to be laid on the **seabed** (ground mine) in **shallow or medium-depth waters**, making it extremely difficult for enemy minesweepers to detect and neutralize.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technical Specifications:** The full-scale version of these mines typically carries a high-explosive warhead of approximately **480 kg to 500 kg**, capable of crippling large warships.
 
• **Operational Life:** These indigenous mines are designed with a **shelf life** of over **10 to 15 years** and can remain active on the seabed for long durations (up to **one year**) after deployment.
 
• **Safety Features:** The mines include **advanced arming and safety devices** to ensure they only become active after reaching a specific depth and after a pre-set time delay, preventing accidents during deployment by **Indian Navy** personnel.
 
• **Context of Trial:** The **May 2025** trial marks the final stages of **user validation trials** before the weapon system is formally inducted into the permanent arsenal of the **Indian Navy**.
